champion: Abdominal distension due to ovarian mass
ordered_diagnoses: Abdominal distension due to ovarian mass

facts.raw_span: a two-year history of gradually progressive abdominal distension
denied pain, vaginal bleeding, or systemic symptoms
no personal or family history of cancer
BMI was 20.5 kg/m2
blood pressure 125/85 mmHg
pulse 89/min
SpO2 95% on room air
abdomen was markedly distended with a palpable mass rising approximately 3 cm above the umbilicus
Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrated an 18 cm diameter ovarian tumor
hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL with a microcytic profile (MCV 73.2 fL)

Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a large, fluid-filled lesion measuring 19.3 × 6.2 × 21 cm, located in the pelvis and mid-abdomen, displacing the uterus and compressing the aorta and inferior vena cava

The patient has a microcytic anemia with a low hemoglobin level, which is consistent with iron deficiency anemia.

rationales.F01: Abdominal distension is a common symptom of ovarian masses.
rationales.F08: A palpable mass in the abdomen is highly suggestive of an ovarian tumor.
rationales.F09: An 18cm diameter ovarian tumor is highly indicative of a malignant or benign ovarian neoplasm.
rationales.F10: Microcytic anemia is often associated with iron deficiency anemia.
rationales.F11: Elevated HE4 levels are associated with ovarian cancer, particularly serous and mucinous subtypes.
rationales.F12: A large, fluid-filled lesion in the pelvis and mid-abdomen is consistent with an ovarian cyst or tumor.
